title: Wound Types, Healing, and the PCP Wound Assessment
next: Chapter 22, Lesson 2: Dressings, Special Wounds, Crush and Blast Injuries

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already dress wounds, control bleeding and check distal circulation. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Use skin and healing basics to predict infection and poor healing
  2. Name the wound types, and spot the ones worse than they look
  3. Run a PCP-level wound assessment: priorities, history, reassessment

Textbook: Chapter 22, PDF pages 1814–1851
slides.say: Welcome to Chapter twenty-two, soft-tissue injuries. These are the most common injuries you'll see, and as an EMR you've treated plenty: you dress them, control the bleeding, and check the circulation beyond the wound. As a PCP, the hands-on part changes less than the thinking. You're expected to predict which wounds will get infected or heal badly, to recognize injuries that are worse than they look, and to take a deeper history. Today we cover three things: skin and healing basics, the wound types, and a PCP-level wound assessment.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来到第二十二章，软组织损伤。这是你最常遇到的损伤，作为 EMR 你已经处理过很多：包扎、止血、检查伤口远端的循环。作为 PCP，动手的部分变化不大，变的是思考：你要能预判哪些伤口会感染或愈合不好，认出那些比看上去更严重的损伤，病史也要问得更深。今天讲三件事：皮肤和愈合的基础、伤口类型，以及 PCP 层级的伤口评估。

slides.title: The skin: layers and jobs
slides.body:
Epidermis5 layers; surface is dead cellsfirst barrier
Dermiscollagen, nerves, vessels, glandsstrength, sensation
Subcutaneousmostly fatinsulation, cushion
  • Below the fat: deep fascia, a tough sheet around the muscles
  • Big skin loss → infection, heat loss, fluid problems
  • Wounds across tension lines gape and heal slowly
slides.say: A quick rebuild of the skin, because it explains what you'll see. The epidermis has five layers, and its surface is dead cells that keep falling off and being replaced. Below it, the dermis holds the collagen that makes skin strong, plus nerves, vessels, and sweat glands. Under that is the subcutaneous layer, mostly fat. Below the fat is the deep fascia, a tough sheet around the muscles; remember it for later. Skin keeps germs out, controls temperature, holds fluid in, and senses pain. So when a lot of skin is lost, expect infection, heat loss, and fluid problems. And a wound that runs across the skin's tension lines gapes open and heals slowly.
slides.sayZh: 快速复习一下皮肤，它能解释你看到的很多现象。表皮有五层，表面是不断脱落、不断更新的死细胞。下面是真皮，含有让皮肤结实的胶原，还有神经、血管和汗腺。再往下是皮下组织，主要是脂肪。脂肪下面是深筋膜，一层包着肌肉的坚韧薄膜，后面会用到。皮肤负责挡住细菌、调节体温、保住体液、感知疼痛。所以大面积皮肤缺损时，要预料到感染、失温和体液问题。另外，横跨皮肤张力线的伤口会裂开，愈合也慢。

slides.title: How wounds heal, and what slows it
slides.body:
Hemostasis→Inflammation→New skin, new vessels→Collagen
  • New vessels are fragile; a scar is weaker than the original skin
  • Drugs that slow it: steroids, NSAIDs, anticoagulants, immunosuppressants
  • Also slowed by age, diabetes, alcoholism, poor circulation
  • Most open wounds should be closed within 6 to 8 hours
slides.say: Healing happens in overlapping stages. First, hemostasis: vessels clamp down, platelets plug the hole, and a clot forms. Then inflammation: white cells arrive to clean up, which is why a healing wound is red, swollen, warm, and sore. Next, new skin cells cover the wound and new vessels grow in, and finally collagen pulls the edges together. The scar is never as strong as the original skin. Here's the PCP angle: the medication history tells you who will heal badly. Steroids, anti-inflammatories, blood thinners, and immune-suppressing drugs all slow healing, and so do older age, diabetes, alcoholism, and poor circulation. Most open wounds should be closed within six to eight hours.
slides.sayZh: 愈合分几个互相重叠的阶段。先是止血：血管收缩，血小板堵住破口，形成血凝块。然后是炎症：白细胞赶来清理，所以愈合中的伤口会红、肿、热、痛。接着新的皮肤细胞覆盖创面、新血管长进来，最后胶原把创缘拉拢。瘢痕永远没有原来的皮肤结实。PCP 的角度在这里：用药史能告诉你谁会愈合不好。激素、消炎止痛药、抗凝药、免疫抑制药都会拖慢愈合，高龄、糖尿病、酗酒、循环差也一样。多数开放伤口应在六到八小时内闭合。

slides.title: Infection: wounds that go bad later
slides.body:
• Signs appear days later: redness, pus, warmth, swelling, pain
  • Red streak up the limb = lymphangitis (spreading infection)
  • Fever, chills, low BP → the infection has gone systemic
  • High risk: bites, embedded or organic material, injections, crush
  • Tetanus: ask about the last shot; booster every 10 years

Necrotizing fasciitis: pain far worse than the wound looks; mortality 20–80%. Use contact and droplet precautions.
slides.say: Infection usually appears days after the injury. Look for redness, pus, warmth, swelling, and pain. A red streak running up the limb is lymphangitis: the infection is spreading along the lymph channels. Fever, chills, or a falling blood pressure mean it has gone systemic. Some wounds are high risk from the start: human and animal bites, embedded or organic material, injection injuries, and crush wounds. Ask when the patient last had a tetanus shot; in Canada a booster is due every ten years. And know necrotizing fasciitis: severe pain far out of proportion to what you see. It kills twenty to eighty percent of patients and is a surgical emergency.
slides.sayZh: 感染通常在受伤几天后才出现。看有没有红、脓、热、肿、痛。沿肢体向上的红线是淋巴管炎，说明感染正沿淋巴管扩散。发热、寒战或血压下降，说明感染已经全身化。有些伤口一开始就是高危：人和动物咬伤、嵌有异物或有机物的伤口、注射伤、挤压伤。要问病人上一次打破伤风针是什么时候；在加拿大每十年要加强一次。还要认识坏死性筋膜炎：疼痛远远超过你看到的伤情。它的死亡率是百分之二十到八十，属于外科急症。

slides.q: Two days after a dog bite on the hand, your patient has a red streak running up the forearm and feels feverish. What does this most likely mean?
options: Normal inflammation of a healing wound
Infection spreading along the lymph channels; this needs hospital care
An allergic reaction to the dressing tape
Early compartment syndrome of the forearm
slides.say: Let's check. Two days after a dog bite on the hand, your patient has a red streak running up the forearm and feels feverish. What does this most likely mean? A, normal inflammation of a healing wound. B, infection spreading along the lymph channels, which needs hospital care. C, an allergic reaction to the dressing tape. D, early compartment syndrome of the forearm. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 检查一下。手被狗咬伤两天后，病人前臂出现一条向上延伸的红线，还觉得发烧。最可能是什么意思？A 伤口愈合中的正常炎症；B 感染正沿淋巴管扩散，需要去医院；C 对敷料胶布过敏；D 前臂早期骨筋膜室综合征。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. A red streak running from a wound is lymphangitis, and fever suggests the infection is spreading through the body. A bite is a high-risk wound from the start. A is wrong because normal inflammation stays around the wound and doesn't cause a streak or fever. C would cause a rash where the tape touched. D causes deep, severe pain in a tight compartment, not a red streak.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。从伤口延伸出的红线是淋巴管炎，发热提示感染正在向全身扩散。咬伤一开始就是高危伤口。A 错在正常炎症只局限在伤口周围，不会出现红线和发热；C 会在胶布贴过的地方出疹；D 的表现是绷紧的筋膜室里深部剧痛，不是红线。

slides.title: Closed vs open wounds
slides.body:
ClosedOpen
Skinintactbroken
Examplescontusion, hematomaabrasion, laceration, puncture
Infectionlow riskalready contaminated
Bleedinglimited by pressure (leg: up to about 2 L)can drain the whole blood volume
slides.say: Every soft-tissue wound is closed or open. In a closed wound, the skin is intact but the tissue underneath is damaged. A contusion, or bruise, causes pain and swelling. Small vessels bleeding in the dermis cause ecchymosis, the blue-black colour, and a bigger vessel can form a hematoma, a lump of pooled blood. Open wounds are more dangerous for two reasons. First, they're already contaminated, so infection depends on how they're managed. Second, bleeding has no limit. A closed leg injury can hold up to about two litres before the pressure stops it, but an open wound can drain the patient's entire blood volume.
slides.sayZh: 软组织伤口分闭合和开放两类。闭合伤皮肤完整，但下面的组织受了伤。挫伤，也就是瘀伤，会引起疼痛和肿胀。真皮里的小血管出血形成瘀斑，就是青紫色；较大的血管出血可以形成血肿，也就是积血的肿块。开放伤更危险，原因有两个。第一，伤口已经被污染，会不会感染取决于怎么处理。第二，出血没有上限。闭合的腿伤最多能藏约两升血，之后压力会把出血压住；但开放伤口可以让病人流光全身的血。

slides.title: Open wounds: know the types
slides.body:
• Abrasion: surface scraped off, painful, dirty; don't scrub on scene
  • Laceration (jagged) vs incision (clean); check distal PMS
  • Puncture: little bleeding outside, maybe deep damage and shock
  • Avulsion: flap torn loose; a kinked flap loses its blood supply
  • Amputation: clean cuts bleed less than crushing or tearing
  • Degloving: skin stripped off the hand like a glove
slides.say: Here are the open wound types. An abrasion is a scrape: painful and often dirty, but don't try to scrub it on scene; at most, cover it lightly. A laceration is a jagged cut, and an incision is a clean one, which heals better. For any deep cut, check pulse, movement, and sensation beyond it. A puncture looks small and bleeds little outside, but it can hide deep, fatal damage, so think internal injury and shock. An avulsion is a flap of skin torn loose; if the flap is folded or twisted, it loses its blood supply. In an amputation, a clean cut often bleeds less than you'd expect, while crushing or tearing can be deadly.
slides.sayZh: 开放伤口有这几类。擦伤是刮蹭伤，很痛、常常很脏，但不要在现场刷洗，最多轻轻盖上敷料。裂伤是边缘参差的伤口，切割伤边缘整齐，愈合更好。凡是深的伤口，都要查远端的脉搏、运动和感觉。刺伤看上去很小、外出血少，却可能藏着致命的深部损伤，所以要想到内伤和休克。撕脱伤是一块皮瓣被撕开；皮瓣如果被折叠或扭转，就会断了血供。离断伤里，锐器切断的出血往往比你想的少，而挤压或撕扯造成的离断可能致命。

slides.title: Compartment syndrome
slides.body:
Pain out of proportion → think compartment syndrome

  • Fascia doesn't stretch: swelling or bleeding raises the pressure
  • Earliest sign: pain worse than the injury, not eased by analgesia
  • Pain gets worse with passive stretch of the muscle
  • Pulse, colour, temperature, sensation changes are very late
  • Over 6 hours: serious risk of tissue death
slides.say: Remember the deep fascia? Limb muscles sit in compartments wrapped by this tough sheet, and it doesn't stretch. After a fracture or a crush, swelling and bleeding raise the pressure inside until blood can't get in. That's compartment syndrome. You may learn six Ps, but by the time the pulse, colour, temperature, or sensation change, it's very late. The first sign is pain out of proportion to the injury, not relieved by pain medication, and worse when you passively stretch the muscle, for example bending the foot upward to stretch the calf. After six hours there's serious risk of tissue death, and only surgery fixes it.
slides.sayZh: 还记得深筋膜吗？四肢的肌肉被这层坚韧的膜包成一个个筋膜室，而它不能伸展。骨折或挤压之后，肿胀和出血让室内压力升高，直到血流进不去，这就是骨筋膜室综合征。你可能学过「六个 P」，但等到脉搏、颜色、皮温、感觉都变了，已经非常晚。最早的信号是与伤情不相称的疼痛：止痛药无效，被动牵拉肌肉时加重，比如把脚往上扳去牵拉小腿。超过六小时，组织坏死的风险很大，只有手术能解决。

slides.q: Your patient has a splinted lower-leg fracture. Twenty minutes later the pain is getting worse despite Entonox, and gently bending the foot upward makes it much worse. The foot pulse is still strong. What is your best interpretation?
options: The splint is working; the strong pulse rules out a circulation problem
Suspect compartment syndrome: loosen anything tight, keep reassessing, and tell the hospital
Normal fracture pain: give more Entonox and stop reassessing
Remove the splint so the patient can move the leg
slides.say: Here's an assessment question. Your patient has a splinted lower-leg fracture. Twenty minutes later, the pain is getting worse despite Entonox, and gently bending the foot upward makes it much worse. The foot pulse is still strong. What's your best interpretation? A, the splint is working, and the strong pulse rules out a circulation problem. B, suspect compartment syndrome: loosen anything tight, keep reassessing, and tell the hospital. C, normal fracture pain: give more Entonox and stop reassessing. D, remove the splint so the patient can move the leg. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道评估题。病人小腿骨折已上夹板。二十分钟后，用了笑气疼痛仍越来越重，轻轻把脚往上扳时疼得更厉害。足背动脉搏动仍然有力。你最好的判断是什么？A 夹板有效，脉搏有力就排除了循环问题；B 怀疑骨筋膜室综合征：松开过紧的包扎，持续复评，并告知医院；C 这是正常骨折疼痛，再给笑气，不用再复评；D 拆掉夹板让病人活动小腿。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Pain out of proportion, not relieved by analgesia, and worse with passive stretch is the early picture of compartment syndrome. A is the classic trap: a strong pulse doesn't rule it out, because pulse loss is a very late sign. C ignores a red flag. D removes the immobilization and causes more harm. Loosen anything tight, keep checking distal circulation, and report it so the hospital can act early.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。与伤情不相称、止痛无效、被动牵拉加重的疼痛，正是骨筋膜室综合征的早期表现。A 是经典陷阱：脉搏有力并不能排除，因为脉搏消失是非常晚期的征象。C 忽略了危险信号。D 拆掉固定只会造成更多伤害。松开过紧的东西，持续检查远端循环，并报告医院，让医院尽早处理。

slides.title: Assessment: the wound can wait
slides.body:
• Scene: traffic, second devices after explosions, body fluids
  • Primary survey first: airway, breathing, major bleeding
  • Major MOI → rapid trauma assessment with DCAP-BTLS
  • Blood on your gloves = a wound you haven't found yet
  • Check the neck before the collar goes on
  • Aim for under 10 minutes on scene; finish the exam en route
slides.say: Soft-tissue wounds can look dramatic, but they're rarely what kills first, so keep your order. Make the scene safe: traffic at a collision, a possible second device at a deliberate explosion, and blood exposure. In the primary survey, airway, breathing, and major bleeding come before any dressing. With a significant mechanism, do a rapid trauma assessment, looking for DCAP-BTLS: deformities, contusions, abrasions, punctures, burns, tenderness, lacerations, and swelling. Blood on your gloves means a wound you haven't found. Examine the neck before the collar hides it. And aim for less than ten minutes on scene; the detailed exam happens en route.
slides.sayZh: 软组织伤口看上去吓人，但很少是最先致命的，所以要守住顺序。先确保现场安全：车祸要防车流，蓄意爆炸要防第二个爆炸装置，还要防血液暴露。初步评估时，气道、呼吸和大出血都排在任何包扎之前。受伤机制严重时，做快速创伤评估，按 DCAP-BTLS 查：畸形、挫伤、擦伤、刺伤、烧伤、压痛、裂伤、肿胀。手套上有血，说明有你还没找到的伤口。戴颈托之前先把颈部查完。现场时间争取少于十分钟，详细查体放在路上做。

slides.title: Your PCP history and reassessment
slides.body:
• MOI: speed, seat belt, fall height, landing surface, weapon
  • Anticoagulants first: warfarin, dabigatran, rivaroxaban, apixaban
  • Antiplatelets: aspirin, clopidogrel, ticagrelor
  • Date of the last tetanus shot
  • Reassess every 5 min if unstable, every 15 min if stable
  • Gunshot wound: document in detail; you may go to court
slides.say: As a PCP, your history goes deeper. Get the mechanism details: speed, seat belt, fall height, what the patient landed on, and any weapon. Ask about blood thinners, because they decide how much a wound will bleed. The book puts anticoagulants first: warfarin, dabigatran, rivaroxaban, and apixaban. Antiplatelet drugs, like aspirin, clopidogrel, and ticagrelor, also keep wounds oozing. Ask about the last tetanus shot. Reassess every five minutes if the patient is unstable, and every fifteen if stable. And for gunshot wounds, document the scene, the injuries, and your care in detail, because you may be called to court.
slides.sayZh: 作为 PCP，病史要问得更深。问清受伤机制：车速、有没有系安全带、坠落高度、落在什么上面、用了什么凶器。要问抗凝药，因为它决定伤口会出多少血。书上把抗凝药放在首位：华法林、达比加群、利伐沙班、阿哌沙班。抗血小板药，比如阿司匹林、氯吡格雷、替格瑞洛，也会让伤口不停渗血。问上一次打破伤风针的时间。不稳定的病人每五分钟复评一次，稳定的每十五分钟一次。枪伤要把现场、伤情和你的处置详细记录下来，因为你可能要出庭作证。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: the Wound Care protocol
slides.body:
BC Wound Care has no PCP-only section. The PCP difference starts when a wound causes shock.

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Expose and examine; control major hemorrhage
  • Analgesia when appropriate
  • Clean, dress and bandage wounds
  • Cold only if distal circulation is not impaired
  • Assess distal circulation; stabilize embedded objects

PCP adds (Hypovolemia protocol)

  • En route: vascular access
  • Fluid bolus 20 mL/kg, max 2 L, reassess every 500 mL
  • Consider TXA for shock from blood loss or hidden bleeding
  • TXA: not over 3 h, under age 12, or isolated head injury
slides.say: Here's an honest look at the BC Wound Care protocol: it has no PCP-only section. Everything on the left is done the same way by EMRs and PCPs: expose and examine, control major bleeding, give analgesia when appropriate, clean and dress wounds, apply cold only if the circulation beyond the wound is intact, check distal circulation, and stabilize embedded objects. The PCP difference starts when a wound causes shock. Then the hypovolemia protocol applies: en route, start an IV, give twenty millilitres per kilogram up to two litres, reassessing every five hundred, and consider TXA, tranexamic acid, keeping its hard stops in mind.
slides.sayZh: 坦白讲，BC 伤口处理流程没有 PCP 专属的部分。左边这些，EMR 和 PCP 做法完全一样：暴露检查、控制大出血、适当时给镇痛、清洁包扎伤口、只有远端循环正常才冷敷、检查远端循环、原位固定嵌入物。PCP 的不同从伤口导致休克时开始。这时要用低血容量流程：在途中开静脉，按每公斤二十毫升补液、最多两升、每五百毫升复评一次，并考虑 TXA，也就是氨甲环酸，同时记住它的硬禁忌。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Pain: BC scoring expects OPQRRRST or LOTARP
  • Cold: only if distal circulation is intact; early cold needs a side-by-side check
  • Pulseless deformed limb: one attempt to realign it
  • Pulse returns → treat as stable; still pulseless → unstable
  • Embedded objects stay in place unless they impair the airway
slides.say: A few BC points to lock in. For pain, the BC scoring sheets expect either OPQRRRST or LOTARP, so practise one of them until it's automatic. For cold packs, BC allows cold only if the distal circulation isn't impaired. To apply it early, at the end of the primary survey, first compare circulation with the uninjured limb. If a deformed limb has no pulse beyond the injury, BC allows one attempt to realign it to the anatomical position. If the pulse comes back, you can treat the patient as stable; if it doesn't, manage the patient as unstable. And embedded objects stay in place unless they're impairing the airway.
slides.sayZh: 几条 BC 要点要记牢。问疼痛时，BC 评分表要求用 OPQRRRST 或 LOTARP 其中一个，选一个练到脱口而出。冷敷方面，BC 规定只有远端循环没有受损才能冷敷；如果要提前在初级评估结束时冷敷，先和未受伤的一侧比较循环。如果变形的肢体在伤处远端摸不到脉搏，BC 允许尝试一次把它复位到解剖位置。脉搏回来了，可以按稳定病人处理；还是没有，就按不稳定处理。嵌入物要原位固定，除非妨碍气道。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• A strong pulse doesn't rule out compartment syndrome
  • On blood thinners? Expect more bleeding and report it
  • Always transport: bites, punctures, wounds over joints, eye injuries
  • Also: nerve, vessel or tendon damage, heavy dirt, embedded objects
  • Necrotizing fasciitis: contact + droplet precautions; clean the truck
  • Recheck distal circulation after every splint or bandage
slides.say: Now the watch-outs that matter more at PCP level. First, a strong pulse never rules out compartment syndrome; trust the pain pattern. Second, a patient on blood thinners will bleed more and longer, so report it at handover. Third, some wounds always need a hospital, however small: bites, punctures, wounds over joints, eye injuries, heavy contamination, embedded objects, and damage to nerves, vessels, muscles, or tendons. Fourth, if you suspect necrotizing fasciitis, use contact and droplet precautions and clean the ambulance well. Fifth, recheck circulation after every splint or bandage, because swelling makes them tighter over time.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲 PCP 层级更要注意的地方。第一，脉搏有力绝不能排除骨筋膜室综合征，要相信疼痛的特点。第二，用抗凝药的病人出血更多、更久，交接时要报告。第三，有些伤口再小也必须送医院：咬伤、刺伤、关节上方的伤口、眼外伤、重度污染、有嵌入物，以及伤到神经、血管、肌肉或肌腱的。第四，怀疑坏死性筋膜炎时，用接触加飞沫防护，事后彻底清洁救护车。第五，每次上夹板或包扎后都要复查循环，因为肿胀会让它们越来越紧。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Open wounds are contaminated, bleed without limit; bites, punctures go in
  2. Out-of-proportion pain, worse on stretch = compartment syndrome
  3. ABCs first; ask about blood thinners and tetanus; reassess 5–15 min

Next: dressings, special wounds, crush and blast injuries
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: open wounds are already contaminated and can bleed without limit, and bites and punctures always need hospital care. Two: pain out of proportion, worse with passive stretch and not relieved by medication, means compartment syndrome until proven otherwise, even with a good pulse. Three: your PCP assessment puts the ABCs before the wound, asks about blood thinners and tetanus, and reassesses every five minutes if unstable and every fifteen if stable. Next lesson: dressings, special wounds like amputations and impaled objects, and crush and blast injuries. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，开放伤口已被污染，出血没有上限；咬伤和刺伤一律要送医院。二，与伤情不相称、被动牵拉加重、止痛无效的疼痛，在排除之前都按骨筋膜室综合征处理，脉搏再好也一样。三，PCP 的评估把 ABC 放在伤口之前，要问抗凝药和破伤风，不稳定每五分钟、稳定每十五分钟复评一次。下节课讲敷料、离断伤和刺入物等特殊伤口，以及挤压伤和爆炸伤。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
